Special Vehicles – Part 2

🪖 Military Convoy

A number of military motor vehicles behind each other, or motor vehicles of the disaster relief organisation.

Military Convoys

To keep a military convoy together as much as possible, they have the following special rights:

🛡️ Special Rights of a Military Convoy
  • Road users must not cut through a military convoy. Once the first vehicle has started crossing or turning, the rest of the convoy may follow — even if other road users have priority. Note: the first vehicle must follow normal traffic rules.
  • They do not have to give way to pedestrians at a pedestrian crossing. All vehicles — including the first — may pass even if pedestrians are waiting.
  • They do not have to give way to buses leaving a bus stop within a built-up area.
  • If the first vehicle crosses an intersection on green, all following vehicles may drive on — even through yellow or red. If other road users have a green light, they must wait until the convoy has finished crossing. Note: the first vehicle must obey the traffic lights.
⚠ First Vehicle Exception

The special rights (cutting through + driving on at red) apply only to the following support vehicles — not the driver of the first vehicle. The first vehicle must always obey normal traffic rules and traffic lights.

Convoy Identification Marks

Vehicles in military convoys carry identification marks — flags and translucent headlamp hoods — to indicate whether they are the first, middle, or last vehicle.

First vehicle Middle vehicle(s) Last vehicle
Flags Two blue
left & right		 One blue
right only		 One green
right only
Headlamp hood One blue
right only		 One blue
right only		 One green
right only

Funeral Procession of Motor Vehicles

🏴 Recognition: Black flag with three white horizontal lines A procession of motor vehicles accompanying a deceased person to a cemetery or crematorium. Motor vehicles that are part of a funeral procession can be recognised by this flag.

Funeral processions have almost the same rights as a military convoy, so following vehicles can continue to follow the hearse as much as possible:

⚫ Special Rights of a Funeral Procession
  • Must not be cut through. The hearse, however, must always follow the traffic rules regarding priority.
  • Do not have to give way to pedestrians at a pedestrian crossing. This applies even to the hearse.
  • Do not have to give way to buses leaving a bus stop. This also includes the hearse.
⚠ Key Difference from Military Convoys — Traffic Lights

Unlike military convoys, following vehicles in a funeral procession must always stop at a yellow or red traffic light — even if the hearse has already entered the intersection on green. They do not have the right to follow through a red light.

🪖
Military Convoy
  • Cannot be cut through ✔
  • No pedestrian crossing give-way ✔
  • No bus stop give-way ✔
  • Following vehicles may cross on red if first entered on green ✔
⚫
Funeral Procession
  • Cannot be cut through ✔
  • No pedestrian crossing give-way ✔
  • No bus stop give-way ✔
  • Following vehicles must stop at yellow/red — no red-light exception ✕

Merging and Overtaking

If you are merging onto an autoweg or motorway and end up next to a military convoy or funeral procession — and it is not possible to merge in front of or behind it — you may merge between the vehicles. Likewise, if you are unable to overtake the entire convoy or procession at once, you may drive in between the vehicles.

ℹ Important Note

If you drive between convoy or procession vehicles, you do not become part of it. You must still follow all normal traffic rules. As this causes inconvenience, avoid it as much as possible.

📋 Priority Signs Take Precedence

The no-cutting rule applies to traffic rules regarding priority (right from right, through traffic, short/long turn). Once priority signs or markings (e.g. priority triangles) are present, these take precedence over those rules — and over the no-cutting rule. Military convoy and funeral procession vehicles must still obey priority signs when approaching them.
